title: End a compressed message without closing the connection

blocks.text: The warehouse service sends stock reports to its branch servers over long-lived connections, one gzip-compressed message after another on the same stream. When `send(...)` returns, the server writes the next message on that connection. Since the reports moved to gzip, some branches see the next message fail on a closed connection, and others get a report that is cut short.

`ReportResponder.send(...)` already builds the layers and writes the rows. Finish `complete(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ReportResponder.java`, so that the branch receives every row of a short or a long report as one complete gzip body, and the connection is still usable afterwards. About two lines in total.

cases.says: the message body starts with the gzip header
send() leaves the connection open, so the server can write its next message on it
every row reaches the client, including the ones still held by the writer when the report ends
the body is complete gzip data that the client can decompress to its end

origin.section: finish() Completes the GZIP Data Without Closing, but Only What Has Reached the Compressor

concepts: close() on a decorator flushes it and closes the stream it wraps, so closing the outermost stream writes every layer's bytes and closes everything below, while closing or flushing only an inner layer leaves data behind.
GZIPOutputStream.finish() completes the compressed data and writes the trailer without closing, but only for what has reached it: layers above must be flushed before it and layers below after it.
